newsitem.title: KENYA: Activity at Nairobi bourse eases on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: Activity at Nairobi bourse eases on tight supply.

text.p: Activity on the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) eased on Thursday due to tight supply on the market, bourse officials said.
The index shed 4.16 points to stand at 3,052.69. Turnover was posted at 9.140 million shillings traded on 209,153 shares from 14.293 million shillings traded on 428,840 shares on Wednesday.
Bourse officials said the market was moderately active with trading concentrated on the normal board. On average, prices on key shares in the market lost marginally.
Uchumi Supermarket eased to 43.50 from 43.75, while Barclays Bank was unchanged at 97. Standard Chartered Bank traded unchanged at 46.75, while Kenya Power & Lighting eased 2 to close at 140.
"Supply in the market is quite tight. Prices across the board are so low that most people are not willing to sell them at this point," a senior broker said.
"In fact, what's been happening in the market is quite interesting -- foreign demand has supported a few shares in the market, driving the prices up," another broker said.
"What we expect to see though, as the year draws to an end, is that prices will start rising on other shares especially those which announce their year-end results around this time," he added.
In the financials, activity has picked up in the last two weeks on Barclays Bank and Standard Chartered Bank shares, whose results are expected any time before the year ends.
Kenya Airways traded at an all-time low of 8.50 from 8.85.
Some brokers said speculators had hoped to make a "quick kill" and had invested heavily in this share. They had now resorted to offloading the share, regardless of the price.
Demand was unmatched at Kenya Commercial Bank, where 50,294 shares were traded at 65.50 from 64.
Foreign investors bought 2,300 shares of Diamond Trust Bank Kenya at 33 from 33.75 and 8,000 shares of National Industrial Credit at 42 unchanged.
